items.note: Pulled 18 in, 38 out in 28s. White peach and cocoa with a whisper of star anise — makes a lovely flat white.

items.note: Moka pot was the wrong call for this anaerobic Sidama — the grapefruit and redcurrant went sharp and boozy. Disappointing.
Cold brewed the Slack Tide blend 18 hours — deep cocoa and caramel, that nutty roundness, zero bitterness. Perfect.
Subscription bag, no roast date on it. The berries and florals are there but it ran a bit thin pulled as espresso.
Pulled 18 in, 38 out in 28s. White peach and cocoa with a whisper of star anise — makes a lovely flat white.
Genuinely can't tell it's decaf — red fruits and mandarin, sugar-cane sweetness. Clean and easy. Eleven days off roast.
Orange and dark caramel, that bakers-chocolate depth in a syrupy body. Only had a best-before so the age is a guess.
Tidewater's Slack Tide in the Aeropress — cocoa and caramel with a nutty finish. Easy-drinking, holds up at twelve days off roast.
Day-five Guji and it's singing — berries and milk chocolate up front, a soft floral lift on the finish. Light and clean.
Homemade oat chai on a cold morning. Cosy enough that I skipped the coffee.
Best latte in the CBD — The Larder Room dials the Lantern Bay Guji in beautifully.
Good latte — Copperline clearly know their Lantern Bay.
Whisked an almond matcha latte at home — finally got the foam (and the heart) right.
Iced oat matcha at Copperline when I'd hit my coffee limit — grassy, clean, just sweet enough.
Straight espresso of the Guji — berries and milk chocolate, lovely crema.
Flat white at The Larder Room — the Guji makes a chocolatey, sweet cup.
Long black at Little Fern — bright and tea-like.
Espresso of the Slack Tide blend at Tidewater's own bar — cocoa, caramel, perfectly pulled.
Pulled as espresso — syrupy and sweet with a balanced crema.
Clean pour-over: bright up front, smooth sweet finish.
